name: Institutional obsolescence

subjectOf.text: Monetary policy instruments become ceremonial under AI driven production, because central banks inject liquidity on schedules calibrated for scarcity economies while production compounds exponentially and money supply grows only linearly.
subjectOf.abstract: Central banks inject liquidity on schedules calibrated for scarcity economies—quarterly adjustments, annual targets, multi-year policy frameworks. Against AI production scaling, these instruments become ceremonial.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Collapse of Scarcity Economics (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6421319
scope_conditions: holds where AI production scales exponentially
holds for central bank toolkits calibrated to constrained labor and limited output

subjectOf.text: Newspapers, record labels, broadcast networks, and publishing houses did not merely lose market share under zero marginal cost distribution; their foundational business models became structurally incoherent because those models assumed distribution was scarce and costly.
subjectOf.abstract: Their foundational business models, built on the assumption that distribution was scarce and costly, became structurally incoherent.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Collapse of Scarcity Economics (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6421319
scope_conditions: observed in the internet content economy
